requirements.quote:
On receipt of DISCONNECT the Server:
MUST discard any Will Message associated with the current connection without publishing it, as described in Section 3.1.2.5 [MQTT-3.14.4-3].
SHOULD close the Network Connection if the Client has not already done so.
requirements.condition: When the Server receives DISCONNECT on a connection with an associated Will Message
requirements.required_behavior: Discard that Will Message.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not retain the Will for later publication.
requirements.why_checkable: Server Will state can be inspected after a graceful DISCONNECT.

requirements.quote:
On receipt of DISCONNECT the Server:
MUST discard any Will Message associated with the current connection without publishing it, as described in Section 3.1.2.5 [MQTT-3.14.4-3].
SHOULD close the Network Connection if the Client has not already done so.
requirements.condition: When the Server receives DISCONNECT on a connection with an associated Will Message
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not publish the discarded Will Message.
requirements.why_checkable: A subscriber can monitor the Will Topic after graceful DISCONNECT for absence of publication.

requirements.quote:
On receipt of DISCONNECT the Server:
MUST discard any Will Message associated with the current connection without publishing it, as described in Section 3.1.2.5 [MQTT-3.14.4-3].
SHOULD close the Network Connection if the Client has not already done so.
requirements.condition: When the Server receives DISCONNECT and the Client has not already closed the Network Connection
requirements.required_behavior: The Server should close the Network Connection.
requirements.why_checkable: Connection state after DISCONNECT can be observed.

requirements.quote: It is necessary for the Client and Server to store Session state in order to provide Quality of Service guarantees. The Client and Server MUST store Session state for the entire duration of the Session [MQTT-4.1.0-1]. A Session MUST last at least as long it has an active Network Connection [MQTT-4.1.0-2].
requirements.condition: For the entire duration of an MQTT Session
requirements.required_behavior: The Client must store its Session state.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not discard required Client Session state while the Session continues.
requirements.why_checkable: Reconnect and in-flight QoS behavior can reveal whether Client state persisted for the full Session.

requirements.quote: It is necessary for the Client and Server to store Session state in order to provide Quality of Service guarantees. The Client and Server MUST store Session state for the entire duration of the Session [MQTT-4.1.0-1]. A Session MUST last at least as long it has an active Network Connection [MQTT-4.1.0-2].
requirements.condition: For the entire duration of an MQTT Session
requirements.required_behavior: The Server must store its Session state.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not discard required Server Session state while the Session continues.
requirements.why_checkable: Reconnect and queued/in-flight QoS behavior can reveal whether Server state persisted for the full Session.

requirements.quote: It is necessary for the Client and Server to store Session state in order to provide Quality of Service guarantees. The Client and Server MUST store Session state for the entire duration of the Session [MQTT-4.1.0-1]. A Session MUST last at least as long it has an active Network Connection [MQTT-4.1.0-2].
requirements.condition: While a Session has an active Network Connection
requirements.required_behavior: Keep the Session active.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not terminate the Session before its active Network Connection ends.
requirements.why_checkable: Session state can be checked throughout the lifetime of an active connection.

requirements.quote: Retained messages do not form part of the Session state in the Server. The Server SHOULD retain such messages until deleted by a Client.
requirements.condition: When the Server stores a retained message
requirements.required_behavior: Keep it outside per-Session state.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not classify the retained message as Session state.
requirements.why_checkable: Terminating a Session and inspecting the retained-message store can distinguish the two state classes.

requirements.quote: Retained messages do not form part of the Session state in the Server. The Server SHOULD retain such messages until deleted by a Client.
requirements.condition: After the Server stores a retained message and before a Client deletes it
requirements.required_behavior: The Server should retain the message.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not discard it merely because a Session ends.
requirements.why_checkable: A later subscription before deletion can test retained-message persistence.

requirements.quote: The MQTT protocol requires an underlying transport that provides an ordered, lossless, stream of bytes from the Client to Server and Server to Client.
requirements.condition: For the underlying transport used by MQTT
requirements.required_behavior: Preserve byte order.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not reorder bytes.
requirements.why_checkable: Known byte sequences can be transmitted and their receive order compared.

requirements.quote: The MQTT protocol requires an underlying transport that provides an ordered, lossless, stream of bytes from the Client to Server and Server to Client.
requirements.condition: For the underlying transport used by MQTT
requirements.required_behavior: Provide lossless byte delivery.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not silently lose bytes within an established transport stream.
requirements.why_checkable: Injected byte sequences can be checked for complete delivery or explicit connection failure.

requirements.quote: The MQTT protocol requires an underlying transport that provides an ordered, lossless, stream of bytes from the Client to Server and Server to Client.
requirements.condition: For the underlying transport used by MQTT
requirements.required_behavior: Provide a byte stream from Client to Server.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not use a transport that lacks Client-to-Server delivery.
requirements.why_checkable: A Client can transmit bytes and Server receipt can be observed.

requirements.quote: The MQTT protocol requires an underlying transport that provides an ordered, lossless, stream of bytes from the Client to Server and Server to Client.
requirements.condition: For the underlying transport used by MQTT
requirements.required_behavior: Provide a byte stream from Server to Client.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not use a transport that lacks Server-to-Client delivery.
requirements.why_checkable: A Server can transmit bytes and Client receipt can be observed.

requirements.quote: Connectionless network transports such as User Datagram Protocol (UDP) are not suitable on their own because they might lose or reorder data.
requirements.condition: When selecting a connectionless or potentially lossy/reordering network transport for MQTT
requirements.required_behavior: Add a layer that supplies the required connection, reliability, and ordering properties.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not use UDP or a similar connectionless transport on its own.
requirements.why_checkable: A transport stack can be inspected and tested for the missing ordering and loss-prevention guarantees.

requirements.quote: MQTT delivers Application Messages according to the Quality of Service (QoS) levels defined here. The delivery protocol is symmetric, in the description below the Client and Server can each take the role of either Sender or Receiver. The delivery protocol is concerned solely with the delivery of an application message from a single Sender to a single Receiver. When the Server is delivering an Application Message to more than one Client, each Client is treated independently. The QoS level used to deliver an Application Message outbound to the Client could differ from that of the inbound Application Message.
requirements.condition: When implementing MQTT message delivery
requirements.required_behavior: Support both Client and Server in the Sender role.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not restrict the Sender role to only one endpoint type.
requirements.why_checkable: Both Client-to-Server and Server-to-Client delivery flows can be exercised.

requirements.quote: MQTT delivers Application Messages according to the Quality of Service (QoS) levels defined here. The delivery protocol is symmetric, in the description below the Client and Server can each take the role of either Sender or Receiver. The delivery protocol is concerned solely with the delivery of an application message from a single Sender to a single Receiver. When the Server is delivering an Application Message to more than one Client, each Client is treated independently. The QoS level used to deliver an Application Message outbound to the Client could differ from that of the inbound Application Message.
requirements.condition: When implementing MQTT message delivery
requirements.required_behavior: Support both Client and Server in the Receiver role.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not restrict the Receiver role to only one endpoint type.
requirements.why_checkable: Both Client-to-Server and Server-to-Client delivery flows can be exercised.

requirements.quote: MQTT delivers Application Messages according to the Quality of Service (QoS) levels defined here. The delivery protocol is symmetric, in the description below the Client and Server can each take the role of either Sender or Receiver. The delivery protocol is concerned solely with the delivery of an application message from a single Sender to a single Receiver. When the Server is delivering an Application Message to more than one Client, each Client is treated independently. The QoS level used to deliver an Application Message outbound to the Client could differ from that of the inbound Application Message.
requirements.condition: For each delivery-protocol instance
requirements.required_behavior: Track delivery from one Sender to one Receiver.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not merge multiple receivers into a single protocol state instance.
requirements.why_checkable: Per-peer identifiers, acknowledgements, and delivery state can be inspected.

requirements.quote: MQTT delivers Application Messages according to the Quality of Service (QoS) levels defined here. The delivery protocol is symmetric, in the description below the Client and Server can each take the role of either Sender or Receiver. The delivery protocol is concerned solely with the delivery of an application message from a single Sender to a single Receiver. When the Server is delivering an Application Message to more than one Client, each Client is treated independently. The QoS level used to deliver an Application Message outbound to the Client could differ from that of the inbound Application Message.
requirements.condition: When the Server delivers one Application Message to multiple Clients
requirements.required_behavior: Treat each Client's delivery independently.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not let one Client's acknowledgement or failure complete or cancel another Client's delivery.
requirements.why_checkable: Two subscribers can be given different acknowledgement behavior and their delivery states compared.

requirements.quote: MQTT delivers Application Messages according to the Quality of Service (QoS) levels defined here. The delivery protocol is symmetric, in the description below the Client and Server can each take the role of either Sender or Receiver. The delivery protocol is concerned solely with the delivery of an application message from a single Sender to a single Receiver. When the Server is delivering an Application Message to more than one Client, each Client is treated independently. The QoS level used to deliver an Application Message outbound to the Client could differ from that of the inbound Application Message.
requirements.condition: When delivering an outbound Application Message to a Client
requirements.required_behavior: The outbound QoS is permitted to differ from the inbound QoS.
requirements.why_checkable: This statement permits but does not require a QoS change, so it imposes no unique observable outcome.

requirements.quote: The message is delivered according to the capabilities of the underlying network. No response is sent by the receiver and no retry is performed by the sender. The message arrives at the receiver either once or not at all.
requirements.condition: When the Receiver gets a QoS 0 PUBLISH
requirements.required_behavior: Send no acknowledgement response.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not send PUBACK or another delivery acknowledgement.
requirements.why_checkable: The receiver's outbound trace can be checked for absence of a response.

requirements.quote: The message is delivered according to the capabilities of the underlying network. No response is sent by the receiver and no retry is performed by the sender. The message arrives at the receiver either once or not at all.
requirements.condition: When the Sender has sent a QoS 0 PUBLISH
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not retry that message.
requirements.why_checkable: A dropped delivery can be followed by monitoring for retransmission.

requirements.quote: The message is delivered according to the capabilities of the underlying network. No response is sent by the receiver and no retry is performed by the sender. The message arrives at the receiver either once or not at all.
requirements.condition: For QoS 0 delivery of one Application Message
requirements.required_behavior: Deliver it either once or not at all.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not deliver a duplicate copy caused by the QoS 0 protocol.
requirements.why_checkable: The onward deliveries associated with one PUBLISH can be counted.

requirements.quote:
In the QoS 0 delivery protocol, the Sender
MUST send a PUBLISH packet with QoS=0, DUP=0 [MQTT-4.3.1-1].
requirements.condition: When the Sender initiates QoS 0 delivery
requirements.required_behavior: Send a PUBLISH packet.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not initiate the delivery with another Control Packet type.
requirements.why_checkable: The first packet type in the delivery flow can be observed.

requirements.quote:
In the QoS 0 delivery protocol, the Sender
MUST send a PUBLISH packet with QoS=0, DUP=0 [MQTT-4.3.1-1].
requirements.condition: When the Sender sends the QoS 0 PUBLISH
requirements.required_behavior: Set QoS to 0.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not set QoS to 1, 2, or 3.
requirements.why_checkable: The PUBLISH fixed-header QoS bits can be inspected.

requirements.quote:
In the QoS 0 delivery protocol, the Sender
MUST send a PUBLISH packet with QoS=0, DUP=0 [MQTT-4.3.1-1].
requirements.condition: When the Sender sends the QoS 0 PUBLISH
requirements.required_behavior: Set DUP to 0.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not mark the initial QoS 0 PUBLISH as a duplicate.
requirements.why_checkable: The PUBLISH fixed-header DUP bit can be inspected.

requirements.quote:
In the QoS 0 delivery protocol, the Receiver
Accepts ownership of the message when it receives the PUBLISH packet.
requirements.condition: When the Receiver receives a QoS 0 PUBLISH
requirements.required_behavior: Accept ownership of the Application Message at receipt.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not wait for an acknowledgement exchange before accepting ownership.
requirements.why_checkable: Receiver state and onward delivery can be observed immediately after PUBLISH receipt.

requirements.quote: This quality of service ensures that the message arrives at the receiver at least once. A QoS 1 PUBLISH Packet has a Packet Identifier in its variable header and is acknowledged by a PUBACK Packet. Section 2.3.1 provides more information about Packet Identifiers.
requirements.condition: For QoS 1 delivery of an Application Message
requirements.required_behavior: Deliver the message to the Receiver at least once.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not complete the delivery with zero Receiver arrivals.
requirements.why_checkable: Receiver delivery events for a QoS 1 publication can be counted.

requirements.quote: This quality of service ensures that the message arrives at the receiver at least once. A QoS 1 PUBLISH Packet has a Packet Identifier in its variable header and is acknowledged by a PUBACK Packet. Section 2.3.1 provides more information about Packet Identifiers.
requirements.condition: For every QoS 1 PUBLISH packet
requirements.required_behavior: Include a Packet Identifier in the variable header.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: A QoS 1 PUBLISH without Packet Identifier is forbidden.
requirements.why_checkable: The variable header can be parsed and checked for field presence.

requirements.quote: This quality of service ensures that the message arrives at the receiver at least once. A QoS 1 PUBLISH Packet has a Packet Identifier in its variable header and is acknowledged by a PUBACK Packet. Section 2.3.1 provides more information about Packet Identifiers.
requirements.condition: When acknowledging a QoS 1 PUBLISH
requirements.required_behavior: Use PUBACK.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not use PUBREC or another acknowledgement type.
requirements.why_checkable: The triggering PUBLISH and acknowledgement packet type can be correlated.

requirements.quote:
In the QoS 1 delivery protocol, the Sender
MUST assign an unused Packet Identifier each time it has a new Application Message to publish. 
MUST send a PUBLISH Packet containing this Packet Identifier with QoS=1, DUP=0.
MUST treat the PUBLISH Packet as “unacknowledged” until it has received the corresponding PUBACK packet from the receiver. See Section 4.4 for a discussion of unacknowledged messages.
[MQTT-4.3.2-1].
requirements.condition: Each time the QoS 1 Sender has a new Application Message to publish
requirements.required_behavior: Assign a Packet Identifier.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not send the new message without an identifier.
requirements.why_checkable: Each new-message PUBLISH can be parsed for the identifier field.

requirements.quote:
In the QoS 1 delivery protocol, the Sender
MUST assign an unused Packet Identifier each time it has a new Application Message to publish. 
MUST send a PUBLISH Packet containing this Packet Identifier with QoS=1, DUP=0.
MUST treat the PUBLISH Packet as “unacknowledged” until it has received the corresponding PUBACK packet from the receiver. See Section 4.4 for a discussion of unacknowledged messages.
[MQTT-4.3.2-1].
requirements.condition: When assigning a Packet Identifier to a new QoS 1 Application Message
requirements.required_behavior: Choose an identifier not currently in use by the Sender.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not reuse an identifier that remains assigned to an unacknowledged exchange.
requirements.why_checkable: The set of outstanding Packet Identifiers can be compared with the new assignment.

requirements.quote:
In the QoS 1 delivery protocol, the Sender
MUST assign an unused Packet Identifier each time it has a new Application Message to publish. 
MUST send a PUBLISH Packet containing this Packet Identifier with QoS=1, DUP=0.
MUST treat the PUBLISH Packet as “unacknowledged” until it has received the corresponding PUBACK packet from the receiver. See Section 4.4 for a discussion of unacknowledged messages.
[MQTT-4.3.2-1].
requirements.condition: When sending the initial QoS 1 PUBLISH for a new Application Message
requirements.required_behavior: Include the assigned Packet Identifier.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not substitute a different Packet Identifier.
requirements.why_checkable: The allocated value and serialized variable-header value can be compared.

requirements.quote:
In the QoS 1 delivery protocol, the Sender
MUST assign an unused Packet Identifier each time it has a new Application Message to publish. 
MUST send a PUBLISH Packet containing this Packet Identifier with QoS=1, DUP=0.
MUST treat the PUBLISH Packet as “unacknowledged” until it has received the corresponding PUBACK packet from the receiver. See Section 4.4 for a discussion of unacknowledged messages.
[MQTT-4.3.2-1].
requirements.condition: When sending the initial QoS 1 PUBLISH for a new Application Message
requirements.required_behavior: Set QoS to 1.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not encode another QoS value.
requirements.why_checkable: The PUBLISH QoS bits can be compared with binary 01.

requirements.quote:
In the QoS 1 delivery protocol, the Sender
MUST assign an unused Packet Identifier each time it has a new Application Message to publish. 
MUST send a PUBLISH Packet containing this Packet Identifier with QoS=1, DUP=0.
MUST treat the PUBLISH Packet as “unacknowledged” until it has received the corresponding PUBACK packet from the receiver. See Section 4.4 for a discussion of unacknowledged messages.
[MQTT-4.3.2-1].
requirements.condition: When sending the initial QoS 1 PUBLISH for a new Application Message
requirements.required_behavior: Set DUP to 0.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not mark the initial transmission as a duplicate.
requirements.why_checkable: The PUBLISH DUP bit can be inspected.

requirements.quote:
In the QoS 1 delivery protocol, the Sender
MUST assign an unused Packet Identifier each time it has a new Application Message to publish. 
MUST send a PUBLISH Packet containing this Packet Identifier with QoS=1, DUP=0.
MUST treat the PUBLISH Packet as “unacknowledged” until it has received the corresponding PUBACK packet from the receiver. See Section 4.4 for a discussion of unacknowledged messages.
[MQTT-4.3.2-1].
requirements.condition: After sending a QoS 1 PUBLISH and before its corresponding PUBACK arrives
requirements.required_behavior: Treat the PUBLISH as unacknowledged.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not mark the exchange acknowledged prematurely.
requirements.why_checkable: Sender in-flight state can be inspected while PUBACK is withheld.

requirements.quote:
In the QoS 1 delivery protocol, the Sender
MUST assign an unused Packet Identifier each time it has a new Application Message to publish. 
MUST send a PUBLISH Packet containing this Packet Identifier with QoS=1, DUP=0.
MUST treat the PUBLISH Packet as “unacknowledged” until it has received the corresponding PUBACK packet from the receiver. See Section 4.4 for a discussion of unacknowledged messages.
[MQTT-4.3.2-1].
requirements.condition: When the Receiver's corresponding PUBACK arrives
requirements.required_behavior: End the PUBLISH packet's unacknowledged state.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not let a PUBACK with a different Packet Identifier acknowledge it.
requirements.why_checkable: PUBACK identifiers can be varied and Sender state transitions observed.

requirements.quote: The Packet Identifier becomes available for reuse once the Sender has received the PUBACK Packet.
requirements.condition: After the Sender receives the corresponding PUBACK
requirements.required_behavior: Make that Packet Identifier available for reuse.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not make it available before the acknowledgement is received.
requirements.why_checkable: Identifier allocation before and after PUBACK can be exercised.

requirements.quote: Note that a Sender is permitted to send further PUBLISH Packets with different Packet Identifiers while it is waiting to receive acknowledgements.
requirements.condition: While waiting for acknowledgements
requirements.required_behavior: The Sender is permitted to pipeline further PUBLISH packets.
requirements.why_checkable: This permission imposes no requirement to pipeline and therefore no unique observable outcome.

requirements.quote: Note that a Sender is permitted to send further PUBLISH Packets with different Packet Identifiers while it is waiting to receive acknowledgements.
requirements.condition: If the Sender pipelines further PUBLISH packets while earlier acknowledgements are pending
requirements.required_behavior: Use Packet Identifiers different from those of the pending PUBLISH packets.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not reuse an outstanding Packet Identifier.
requirements.why_checkable: All concurrently outstanding PUBLISH identifiers can be collected and checked for uniqueness.
